result:
There is a fragile, unnamed hour just before the dawn when the city belongs to no one and everyone at once. Streetlights hum their low amber lullabies against wet asphalt, reflecting puddles that mirror an indigo sky devoid of stars. The world is suspended in an intake of breath, holding its pulse between yesterday’s regrets and tomorrow’s relentless demands.

In this stillness, the ordinary transforms into something almost holy. A solitary fox slips between parked sedans like a shadow, untroubled by the mechanics of human ambition. The distant clatter of a night train vibrates through the soles of your shoes, a ghost carrying tired bodies toward unseen destinations. Windows are dark, hiding millions of dreams, arguments, and quiet reconciliations beneath cool brick and pane.

Soon, the spell will shatter. The first delivery trucks will rattle over potholes, the smell of burnt espresso will bleed through café grates, and footsteps will multiply until the quiet is trampled underfoot. Clocks will resume their tyrannies, measuring our worth in minutes and deadlines. But for now, standing on the balcony with cold air biting at bare forearms, there is only the vast, indifferent grace of morning arriving.

The darkness thins to slate, then to a bruised violet, until the highest spire catches the first needle of gold. It asks nothing of you: no productivity, no explanations, no courage. It merely offers another clean slate, blank and cold, patiently waiting for the messy, necessary ink of a brand new human day to begin again below.
